A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe PolyPose. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite title changes and relocated material.

before.justification: v3 reports original Head&Neck and DeepFluoro registration results, quantitative ablations, and a failure-case analysis.

after.justification: v4 retains original registration experiments and adds ThoraxCBCT results, segmentation-corruption experiments, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The polyrigid equations, weighting, losses, and optimization steps remain unchanged. Sections 3.2 and C.1 change the camera-registration attribution from DiffPose [15] to xvr [16], but retain the same procedural description; v3 C.1 already cites both works. The PDFs leave unclear whether the underlying component changed or its attribution was corrected.

E1.justification: Appendix E.3 adds ThoraxCBCT: 13 lung-cancer patients with planning FBCT and interventional CBCT-derived X-rays spanning maximum inhalation and expiration. This substantially extends evaluation to respiratory soft-tissue deformation. Head&Neck, DeepFluoro, and the internal jaw-opening case remain represented.

E2.justification: The matched DeepFluoro training/held-out illustration drops the DiffPose comparator shown in v3 Figure 9 when incorporated into v4 Figure 6. Elsewhere, the rigid comparator is attributed to xvr [16] instead of DiffPose [15], while the other comparison-method families remain.

E3.justification: v4 adds controlled segmentation erosion with a zero-erosion reference, average-runtime evaluation, and the ThoraxCBCT FBCT-to-synthetic-X-ray protocol. The Head&Neck split and viewing settings and DeepFluoro two-input-view/held-out evaluation design remain. v4 does not clearly explain the subject aggregation underlying Table 1.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Figure 7B add a targeted robustness study testing sensitivity to eroded segmentation masks. The deformation-parameterization and weighting ablations remain. The rigid-component ablation moves from v3 Appendix F/Table 5 to v4 Section 4.4/Figure 7A, and the jaw-opening failure analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means, standard deviations, and shaded variability bands. The folding means and SDs appearing in v4 Table 1 already occur in v3 Table 4; added benchmark results follow the existing reporting practice. No changed run counts, seeds, confidence-interval procedures, or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: v4 adds respiratory-registration results, erosion-response curves, and runtimes: PolyPose achieves ThoraxCBCT rigid/soft-tissue Dice of 0.73(0.19)/0.81(0.11), and Figure 5 reports 59 seconds. v3 Table 4's separate Dice/HD95 results for DeepFluoro subjects 2–6 disappear. Table 1 changes Dense R3/anatomix folding values from 0.48%/0.11% to 0.43(0.12)%/3.01(1.21)% while retaining its Dice/HD95 values. Unclear aggregation prevents interpreting these as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations in Equations 1–18 and Appendices A–B remain equivalent, including projective geometry and the SE(3) logarithm/exponential formulas. No new proofs or substantive changes to formal assumptions appear.

C1.justification: The abstract's scientific claims, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same scope: regularization-free polyrigid registration, hyperparameter-free weighting, and accurate sparse-view and limited-angle alignment.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly questions generalization to soft tissue insufficiently constrained by nearby rigid bodies, particularly in the abdomen, and interprets ThoraxCBCT as preliminary support for respiratory registration. Segmentation dependence is discussed alongside the new corruption experiment. The retained jaw-opening limitation now suggests a kinematic-chain extension.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a project-site link advertising code, tutorials, and visualizations. Figure 5 supplies per-method runtimes, and Section 4.1 specifies 24–111 DeepFluoro X-rays per subject. Hardware, Sobel filtering, and optimizer settings were already documented in v3.

R1.justification: v4 adds two ThoraxCBCT dataset references, [68–69], and identifies xvr [16] as the current state-of-the-art rigid comparator. References [15–16] already existed in v3. The related-work survey and broader novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 shortens the title, updates conference and funding text, locally rewrites the DeepFluoro evaluation and discussion, and promotes the rigid-component ablation into the main text. Most introduction, related-work, method, and conclusion prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are substantially reorganized. v4 Figure 6 combines material from v3 Figures 6 and 9; Figure 7 incorporates former Table 5 alongside new erosion plots. Figure 5 gains runtimes, Table 3 gains explicit weight-function/epsilon columns, ThoraxCBCT Figure 11 is added, and v3 Table 4 is removed.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful corruption testing, respiratory-motion evidence, runtimes, resource information, and clearer applicability limits. However, it removes separate DeepFluoro subjects 2–6 accuracy results and the explanation of the single-subject focus. Its Table 1 combines unchanged v3 Table 1 Dice/HD95 values with v3 Table 4 folding statistics without explaining aggregation. These gains in validation and losses in reporting transparency prevent a reliable overall quality judgment.
